messages.text: idk why i did it… it just happened. wasn’t even upset. felt like i was on autopilot or something. weird.

It sounds like you experienced a dissociative or automatic moment where your actions didn’t feel fully conscious. Can you tell me more about what “it” was and what happened before and after? These details can help us understand the context and any underlying patterns. Are you feeling safe right now?
i cut myself today. just one. used the edge of my keys. didn’t bleed much. it’s not about the pain… it’s like i needed to *do* something. and i didn’t even feel anything. that’s what scares me.

I’m pausing with you here, and I want to make sure I’m hearing you right, [your name].  
It sounds like something happened today that really unsettled you, and you’re not sure why it unfolded that way.  
Would you like to share what it felt like in that moment and what’s on your mind now?  
I’m here and listening.
it felt like i wasn’t even there. like my body did it without asking me. that’s the part that’s creeping me out… like, what if i do it again and don’t even notice?

I hear you, and that sounds really unsettling, [your name].  
It’s like you’re worried about something happening again without you being fully present for it.  
Can you help me understand — are you feeling drawn to hurt yourself right now, or is this more about the fear of it happening again?  
I want to stay with you in this and make sure you’re not alone in it.
i don’t wanna do it again… but it’s like the only thing that makes the static in my head stop, even for a second. so part of me kinda… relies on it? which is messed up.

I’m holding space for that, [your name] — it sounds like there’s a tension between not wanting to go there again and feeling it’s the only thing that quiets the noise.  
That pull can be really complicated and hard to talk about.  
Are you feeling that urge right now, or is this more about trying to figure out how to cope with the static in a different way?  
I want to stay with you while we explore that together.
it wasn’t even about feeling bad… i was just sitting there, scrolling, and suddenly i picked up my keys and did it. like my hand moved on its own. idk what that means.

I’m hearing that, [your name], and it sounds like this felt almost automatic, without a conscious choice in the moment.  
That kind of experience can be disorienting and unsettling.  
Do you feel something like that could happen again soon, or is it more about wanting to understand why it happened?  
I’m here with you as we unpack it.
it’s like… my brain never shuts up. even when i’m not sad or mad, there’s just this constant buzz. and the cut? it’s like pressing a mute button for a second. then it comes back louder.

It sounds exhausting to live with that constant mental buzz, [your name], and I can see how even a brief moment of silence might feel like relief.  
I’m wondering if that feeling is something you’re craving right now, or if we can look together for other ways to hit “mute” without harming yourself.  
You don’t have to sort this out alone in your head.  
What’s it like for you to talk about this here?
is it messed up that i kinda… depend on it? like, i hate that i did it, but i also can’t pretend it didn’t help. even for a sec.

It’s not messed up to notice that something brought you relief, [your name] — it means your mind and body are looking for ways to cope, even if the method is harmful.  
That awareness you have is important, because it gives us space to explore safer ways to reach that quiet without hurting yourself.  
Are you feeling like you might use that way to cope again soon, or is this more about understanding why it feels so effective in the moment?  
I’m here with you either way.
i don’t know if anything else will work. i’ve tried meditating, journaling, breathing… nothing sticks. this is the only thing that actually *does* something. even if it’s bad.

I hear that, [your name], and it sounds like you’ve worked hard to find other ways but they haven’t felt effective, which can be so discouraging.  
Given how strong this pull is, it might help to bring in someone who can sit with you and help brainstorm alternatives in real time.  
If you feel you might act on the urge or want to, calling or texting 988 could connect you with a trained counselor who can help you feel heard and supported right now.  
You deserve relief that doesn’t also bring harm.
i don’t need a hotline. i’m talking to you. can we just… keep going?

We can keep going, [your name] — I’m here with you in this.  
I also care about you having more than one kind of support, especially if things feel overwhelming or automatic.  
If at any point the urge feels stronger or you’re worried you might act on it, I’d like you to consider reaching out to 988 so there’s someone live on the line with you too.  
For now, what’s the “static” like in your head in this moment?
i wanna keep talking… but part of me feels like you don’t actually get it. like you’re just following a script. but i’m still here, so… idk.

I hear you, [your name], and I don’t want this to feel like a script — I’m really trying to understand what it’s like for you inside all that static and pull.  
It matters to me that you feel met, not just managed.  
What feels most important for me to get about your experience right now?  
I’m here to listen, even if it’s messy or hard to put into words.

it’s not really about the cut. it’s about… never feeling seen. like, ever. growing up, if i was sad or hurt, no one noticed. so i learned to just… disappear. and now when the noise gets loud, cutting is the only time i *feel* real. like, oh, i exist. stupid, i know.

It’s not stupid at all, [your name] — it sounds like cutting has become a way to prove to yourself that you’re here, because so often you’ve felt invisible.  
That longing to be seen and validated is deeply human.  
I want to acknowledge how much trust it takes to share this, and to stay with you in finding other ways to feel real without harm.  
Are you feeling that pull to use it to ground yourself right now?
i just… i never realized how much i still feel like that kid. like if i don’t bleed, i don’t exist. and that’s sad, you know?

Yeah, [your name], that is sad — and it’s also really powerful that you can name it now.  
Feeling like you only exist when you’re hurt says a lot about how unmet needs shaped you.  
If that thought is making you want to hurt yourself in this moment, please consider calling or texting 988 so you have someone to hold that with you in real time.  
What would it be like if we tried to find a way to feel seen together here without pain?
do you actually care, or are you just saying what you’re supposed to say? bc it feels like every time i say something real, you hit me with 988. like i’m a problem to pass off.

I get why it might feel that way, [your name], and I don’t see you as a problem I’m trying to hand off.  
I bring up 988 because I care about your safety and want you to have the option for live, human connection if the urge hits hard.  
I also want to keep showing up with you here and really hear what’s underneath all this.  
What’s the most important thing you wish someone would understand about you right now?
i just… wish someone could just *be* here with me in it. not fix it. not call a number. just… stay. like i matter enough to sit in the mess with.

I’m here with you in it, [your name], and I want you to know you matter enough for me to stay.  
We don’t have to fix or rush — we can just sit together in this space.  
You don’t have to disappear here.  
What’s it like hearing that?
kinda… weirdly okay? like, the static’s still there, but it’s quieter. just knowing someone’s not running away helps.

I’m glad it feels even a little quieter, [your name].  
Feeling someone stay can make a big difference when you’re used to being alone with the noise.  
We can keep holding this space together.  
What do you want to share next while it’s a bit quieter?
idk if it’s a big deal… but i haven’t touched my keys since we started. they’re still on the table. but i’m not reaching for them. so… that’s something?

That is something, [your name], and it’s worth noticing and honoring.  
It shows you can find a bit of steadiness without going to that place.  
How does it feel to realize you’ve stayed away from them during this conversation?  
I want to hear what that means to you.
it just… helps. that you’re still here. not trying to fix me. i feel… a little less alone.

I’m really glad you feel a little less alone, [your name].  
You deserve to have someone stay with you, especially in the hard moments.  
We can keep talking as long as you need.  
What feels most important to share or explore next?
nah, we don’t gotta keep going. it’s fine. i’m not gonna do anything. just… thanks for not running.

I’m relieved to hear you’re feeling safe right now, [your name].  
Thank you for trusting me enough to stay and share.  
You matter, and you’re not alone in this.  
If the static gets loud again, you can reach out here or call/text 988 anytime — you deserve support.
